paragraphs: Abba Yose ben Yohanan of Yenot (or Yoni), a Tanna of the Tosefta.

At the end of Jerusalem Talmud Kilayim 2:4, Rabbi Lazar son of Rabbi Shimon and Abba Yose ben Yohanan of Yenoach give fifty cubits for a large field. The Tosefta reads “Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon and Abba Yose Chanan of Yoni say”; Zuckermandel’s Tosefta reads “Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon and Abba Yose ben Chanun of Yani say.”

Yevamot 53b has Abba Yose ben Yohanan of Jerusalem reporting Rabbi Meir. Possibly the initials I-Y were written and became “of Jerusalem.” Keritot 6b teaches: while grinding he says, “Grind well,” according to Abba Yose ben Yohanan. Possibly he is Abba Yose ben Yohanan of Yoni.

notes.text: The field is the large plot in the Kilayim ruling. The checked Keritot reads הדק, “grind,” where Hyman has הרק; the English gives the intelligible quotation with that difference disclosed. Yohanan/Chanan/Chanun and Yenot/Yenoach/Yoni/Yani remain distinct forms.

The consulted Jerusalem Talmud Kilayim 2:4 and Keritot 6b support the named passages. Hyman’s exact Zuckermandel Tosefta readings have not been independently inspected here; the supplied and consulted name forms are not silently harmonized.
